title: I.9: Fugue in E major

groocock.chapter: 7 Group 2: Fugues for Three Voices, without Stretto

entries.notes: merges into the countersubject at the third beat of bar 2
real answer; leads via codetta (beats 3-4 of bar 3) to CS at bar 4
extended toward the inverted cadence in the middle of bar 5 (end of exposition)
begins at end of bar 7; followed by codetta (diagram "cod")
begins at end of bar 9; answer once more, with a-natural instead of a-sharp; leads via lengthened codetta into episode 2; diagram key I
leads into CS as part of episode 3
recapitulation; leads into CS as part of episode 4
leads into CS at altered pitch as part of coda; diagram also shows a bracketed [S] in bass in the coda (bar 28)

episodes.material: bass moves from CS figure into figures from the subject; new leaping figure in two-part imitation
11-12 bass develops bass of ep.1 alternating subject and CS figures, upper voices allude to descending scale of bar 7 and leaping figures of ep.1; 13-16 free interchange of 11-12
begins before middle voice finishes its entry; soprano develops leaping figure of ep.1 by inversion
virtually a repeat of latter part of episode 2 with upper voices interchanged

codettas.notes: simple variant of the CS (tone instead of semitone), starting a sequence that pervades the fugue

extensions.to: inverted cadence in middle of bar 5

countersubjects.first: third beat of bar 2 (subject merges into it)
countersubjects.notes: with later entries consists of the repeated figure alone or with part of the following rising scale; interchange interval from list p.13

subject.notes: no obvious ending; presumably overlapped by the answer in bar 2; moto perpetuo from the third note; dominant occurs among first notes but without emphasis, so real answer (p.6)

key_plan: Group 2 table: Exp I V I | Counterexp EP I V I | Dev EP vi | Final EP I V I EP I

claims.claim: Counterexposition bars 6-10 (soprano subject, middle answer, bass answer).
The subject has no obvious ending and is presumably overlapped by the answer in bar 2.
Answer enters just before the subject has finished (I.9 listed among overlapping answers).
From its third note the fugue is a moto perpetuo of semiquavers.
